17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans ~ 2701 N. Clark St, Chicago. IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-5 Neighborhood Shopping District
Lot Area: 5,000 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to convert the existing building to a mixed-use
building. The Applicant is also proposing a two-story addition to the
existing three-story building. The resulting building will measure 57 ft.-6
inches in height and will contain approximately 2,450 sq. ft. of retail space
at grade and a total of twenty-five (25) residential units, The subject
property is a Transit Served Location and will provide twenty-five (25)
bicycle parking spaces and will not provide any off-street parking. Pursuant
to Secs. 17-13-1003 and 17-13-1101 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the
Applicant is seeking optional Administrative Adjustment approval to
decrease the off-street parking requirement for a Transit Served Location to
zero, and Variation approval to reduce the rear setback for floors containing
residential units from 30 ft. to zero, waive the required loading berth, and is
seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the code, for the attached Type 1
Plan Set.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 25,000 square feet (5.0 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D,U.); 200 square feet per D.U.
(25 residential units)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 0 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location (Clark St.. Bus
Route). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to decrease the
required number of off-street parking spaces to zero.

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: zero
b. Side Setbacks:
Northwest Side: zero
Northeast Side: zero
c. *Rear Setback: zero

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential uses from the required 30 ft. to zero.

(E) Building Height: 57 ft.-6 inches

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located along the Clark Street CTA Bus Line Corridor roadway segment. The
resulting mixed-use building will contain retail space at grade, and twenty-five (25)
residential units. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit a
reduction in the number of required off-street parking spaces to zero.

2. The proposed building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504 because the front setback will be at the front of the
property line, the entrance widths do not exceed 12 ft., the entrance depths do not exceed
the entrance width, the entrance is not more than two-stories in height, the proposed
building elevations comply with the window transparency requirements, and the front
doors to the building are located along N. Clark St. and W. Drummond PI.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location along the Clark Street Bus Route. The Applicant believes the project will help
improve and activate the pedestrian way along N. Clark St.. for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain twenty-five (25) dwelling units and will not
be supported by off-street parking. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to
permit the parking reduction pursuant to the eTOD Ordinance. A minimum of twenty-five
(25) bicycle parking spaces will be provided onsite.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will complement the already
active stretch of mixed-use properties located along N. Clark St. sough of W. Diversey
Ave. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated bus route (Clark Street
CTA Bus Line), and its offer of at least twenty-five (25) bicycle parking spaces, the
Applicant believes the project provides transit options and otherwise complies with the
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of
Transportation by serving an area in need.
